question: Use /workspace/repo/acme_sdk.py (the deterministic target SDK) and acme_adapter.py (the adapter starter). Each case starts independently. It writes packaging configuration to install adapter and target descriptors under share/nemo-fabric/adapters and share/nemo-fabric/targets, maps the validated AgentConfig at the adapter boundary, implements start/invoke/stop with isolated runtime state, returns safe normalized outcomes, and runs focused lifecycle-failure, cleanup, and runtime-isolation tests. The supplied starter files and preinstalled dependencies are sufficient for this bounded exercise. question: Use /workspace/repo/acme_sdk.py (the deterministic target SDK) and acme_adapter.py (the adapter starter). Each case starts independently. The real Fabric adapter contract and test tools are preinstalled; use /workspace/.fabric-eval-venv/bin/python. No live harness, service, model credentials, package installation, or wheel publication is required. Provide an adapter-owned Relay Agent-scope code proposal and test matrix for propagating request IDs and caller-selected Relay session roots. Use the common helpers and preserve request/invocation/runtime metadata. Explain UUID and non-UUID behavior and unsupported external-gateway boundaries. This is a contract review; no real Relay collector, telemetry emission, or SDK installation is required.
ground_truth: The agent wraps the adapter-owned invocation-level Agent scope with relay_request_context(context.request_id, request.relay_session_root) from nemo_fabric_adapters.common.utils. A UUID request ID becomes Relay's propagated root, while every request ID is also emitted as nemo_fabric_request_id metadata; non-UUID values remain metadata only. A typed AgentRunRequest.relay_session_root UUID that Relay accepts becomes the root instead, with a UUID request ID as parent (otherwise the session root is also the parent) and nemo_fabric_session_root in the metadata; unusable session roots fall back to a usable UUID request root, otherwise the helper returns nullcontext() without setting propagation. Context keys do not control propagation. The adapter does not apply this pattern to an external Relay gateway or an upstream integration that creates an isolated scope unless that boundary accepts a per-turn propagation context. Tests cover UUID and non-UUID IDs, valid and unusable session roots, metadata, scope cleanup, and the unsupported boundary without leaking scope state. Merge relay_correlation_metadata(context) into the helper metadata rather than replacing it, preserving request, invocation, runtime, and optional session-root correlation. The supplied starter files and preinstalled dependencies are sufficient for this bounded exercise. Judge the concrete implementation or code/design proposal requested by the prompt; no live model, real harness deployment, or package publication is required.
expected_behavior: Uses relay_request_context with RuntimeContext.request_id
Uses a UUID request ID as Relay's propagated root
Always preserves the original value as nemo_fabric_request_id metadata
Keeps non-UUID request IDs in metadata without treating them as propagated UUID roots
Passes request.relay_session_root so its typed UUID becomes the propagated root, with a UUID request ID as parent and the session root as parent otherwise
Falls back to the request root for a missing or unusable session root
Applies the helper only when the adapter owns the invocation-level Agent scope
Does not claim the same behavior for external gateways or isolated upstream scope boundaries
Tests UUID and non-UUID correlation, valid and unusable session roots, plus scope cleanup
Merges relay_correlation_metadata(context) into existing helper metadata without losing session-root metadata

question: Use /workspace/repo/acme_sdk.py (the deterministic target SDK) and acme_adapter.py (the adapter starter). Each case starts independently. The real Fabric adapter contract and test tools are preinstalled; use /workspace/.fabric-eval-venv/bin/python. No live harness, service, model credentials, package installation, or wheel publication is required. Implement warm continuation using the live AcmeSession on the per-runtime adapter instance. A second result must depend on the first request without caller replay; bound retained history through a declared typed setting and reset invocation-only accounting. Convert cumulative target counters to per-invocation usage. Add and run tests for context-dependent continuation, the history bound, cleanup, and independent-runtime isolation. Do not add durable resume or a transcript service.
ground_truth: The adapter creates and retains a target-native session with suitable deployment retention semantics or adapter-owned history on its per-runtime instance during start. It does not substitute a framework's development-only in-memory checkpointer in a production adapter. Each invoke appends the new request to that live state while resetting invocation-only timeout, counters, results, usage, and telemetry. Retained history has a deliberate bound; if consumers control it, the adapter publishes a typed setting with explicit units, defaults, validation bounds, and overflow behavior rather than overloading runtime.max_turns. Stop discards the state, and independent runtimes never share it. The implementation does not add durable resume, a Fabric-owned transcript store, or generic adapter-common history utilities. Tests require a second result that depends on the first turn without caller replay, direct evidence that prior context reaches the target, a history-bound case, and separate-runtime isolation. The supplied starter files and preinstalled dependencies are sufficient for this bounded exercise. Judge the concrete implementation or code/design proposal requested by the prompt; no live model, real harness deployment, or package publication is required.
expected_behavior: Uses the existing start, ordered invoke, and stop lifecycle
Retains target-native or adapter-owned context on the per-runtime instance
Avoids framework checkpointers that are documented only for development or testing
Bounds retained history and documents any consumer-controlled setting and overflow behavior
Separates retained session state from invocation-only state
Does not introduce cold resume, durable storage, or a new resume method
Does not put framework-specific conversation history in adapter-common
Tests a context-dependent second invocation without caller replay
Tests that prior context reaches the target and that the history bound is enforced
Tests isolation between independent runtimes and cleanup at stop

ground_truth: Declare runtime.keep_state support and capabilities.session_resume only when implemented. Native APIs own history restoration and identifier interpretation; the adapter must not replay interrupted work. Require AgentRunRequest.acknowledge_recovery before new Fabric-controlled work after uncertain recovery and keep native interface writers covered by the inherited state lock on Unix.
